 (Bayamón, PR, 1978)
Pintor, escultor, dibujante y artista gráfico. Es egresado de la Escuela Central de Artes Visuales en Santurce, con diploma de escultura. En 1999 ganóla beca Arnaldo Roche con la que viajó a España. En el 2000 terminó su Bachillerato en Artes Gráficas de la Escuela de Artes Plásticas de Puerto Rico y en este mismo año tomó talleres de grabado japonés con el profesor Akiro Kurosaki en Maastrich, Holanda. En el 2005 obtuvo una Maestría en Artes Plásticas de la Universidad Interamericana de Puerto Rico, Recinto de San Germán, en la cual ejerció como profesor de dibujo hasta el 2003. Ha trabajado como asistente del escultor Harry Roseman (en un proyecto de esculturas para el Aeropuerto John F. Kennedy), fue ilustrador del Instituto de Cultura Puertorriqueña y actualmente es profesor de dibujo y pintura de la Escuela de Artes Plásticas de Puerto Rico. Ha expuesto su obra tanto individual como colectivamente en varias actividades de la Isla. Trabaja con imágenes que le rodean a diario, las cuales observa con detenimiento para luego distorsionarlas, añadiéndole movimiento y dinamismo.
Víctor Rodríguez Gotay
 (Bayamón, PR, 1978)
Painter, sculptor, draftsman, and graphic artist. He is a graduate of the Central School of Visual Arts in Santurce, with a diploma in sculpture. In 1999, he won the Arnaldo Roche scholarship and traveled to Spain. In 2000, he completed his Bachelor of Arts in Graphic Arts at the Puerto Rico School of Visual Arts, and that same year he took lessons in Japanese engraving with professor Akiro Kurosaki in Maastrich, Holland. In 2005 he obtained a Master of Arts in Visual Arts from the Inter American University of Puerto Rico, San Germán campus, where he taught drawing until 2003. He has worked as assistant sculptor to Harry Roseman (in a sculpture project at the John F. Kennedy Airport), as illustrator of the Institute of Puerto Rican Culture, and currently as professor of drawing and painting at the Puerto Rico School of Visual Arts. He has exhibited his work, both individually and collectively, in various activities around the Island. He works with the images of his everyday life, observing them in detail and then distorting them by adding movement and dynamism.

inventory.name: Gu Jing Zhou – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Gu Jing Zhou
 (18 October 1915 in Yixing, Jiangsu – 3 June 1996)
Gu Jingzhoe was a Chinese ceramic artist who specialized in the creation of zisha-ware teapots. He was a founder and Deputy Director of Research and Technology at the Number One Yixing Factory. Gu lived in Yixing, a city noted for its pottery. In his early career he worked for an antique dealer named Lang Yushu, and it was during this time that he was exposed to many pieces of classical zisha (purple clay) pottery, a style which he emulated in his own work. He wrote and researched the topic of zisha-ware extensively, and was granted the title “Master of Chinese Industrial Art”.

inventory.name: Henry Moore – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Henry Moore
 (Castleford,1898 – Much Handham,1986)
Escultor. Es uno de los artistas más importantes del siglo veinte. Se formó en la Leeds School of Art y en el Royal Collage of Art. Sus primeras obras denotan un arcaísmo en las que manifiesta sus temas de interés. Para el 1935 se interesó por las ideas surrealistas y la abstracción fusionando ambas. En su etapa de madurez se destacó por la complementariedad entre forma y espacio. Sus obras, de escala monumental, se ubican generalmente en espacios abiertos. Su enfoque se desarrolló a través del estudio del arte monumental del periodo precolombino, egipcio y de la obra del reconocido Miguel Ángel; destacando los materiales y la técnica empleada.
Henry Moore
 (Castleford,1898 – Much Handham,1986)
Sculptor. He is one of the most important artists of the twentieth century. He trained at the Leeds School of Art and the Royal College of Art. His early works denote an archaism in which he manifests his themes of interest. By 1935 he became interested in surrealist ideas and abstraction merging both. In his mature stage he stood out for the complementarity between form and space. His works, monumental in scale, are generally located in open spaces. His approach was developed through the study of monumental art of the pre-Columbian period, Egyptian and the work of the renowned Michelangelo; highlighting the materials and technique used.

inventory.name: Luis Germán Cajiga – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Luis Germán Cajiga
 (Quebradillas, PR, 1934)
Pintor y artista gráfico. En 1952 se trasladó a San Juan donde tuvo a grandes figuras del arte como Lorenzo Homar, Rafael Tufiño, José Meléndez Contreras y Félix Bonilla Norat en el Taller de Artes Gráficas de la División de Educación de la Comunidad (Divedco). Realizó estudios de perspectiva con el pintor Fran Cervoni. De 1960 a 1962 fue asistente de Lorenzo Homar en el Taller de Gráfica del Instituto de Cultura Puertorriqueña. En 1975 obtuvo una Maestría en Educación en la Universidad Interamericana de Puerto Rico y desde 1979 mantiene su galería en el Viejo San Juan. Se ha destacado por una obra costumbrista en la que plasma estampas y paisajes de pueblo, principalmente del Viejo San Juan.
Luis Germán Cajiga
 (Quebradillas, PR, 1934)
Painter and graphic artist. He moved to San Juan in 1952, where his role models included such great artists as Lorenzo Homar, Rafael Tufiño, José Meléndez Contreras, and Félix Bonilla Norat at the Graphic Arts Workshop of the Division of Community Education (Divedco). He studied perspective with painter Fran Cervoni. From 1960 to 1962 he was assistant to Lorenzo Homar at the Graphics Workshop of the Institute of Puerto Rican Culture. In 1975 he obtained a Master of Arts in Education from the Inter American University of Puerto Rico, and since 1979 he has had his own gallery in Old San Juan. His work is renowned for his portrayals of native customs and his depiction of town scenes and sights, mainly of Old San Juan.

inventory.name: Miguel A. Soto Cuevas – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Miguel A. Soto Cuevas
 (1918-2010 Lares, PR)
Arquitecto, Múscio y Artista gráfico. Comenzó sus estudios universitarios en Agronomía en el Colegio de Agricultura y Artes Mecánicas de Mayagüez; conocido hoy en día como el Recinto de Mayagüez, U.P.R. Cantó en el coro y organizó un cuarteto donde era el cantante. También viajó por pueblos y colegios universitarios de la Isla promoviendo al Colegio. Posteriormente, se trasladó a Estados Unidos, donde en 1941 obtuvo un Bachillerato en Educación Industrial con una concentración en Arquitectura de la Universidad de Texas A&M, College Station, Texas. Al regresar a Puerto Rico trabajó como Maestro por un año en Aguadilla. Luego se integró a un grupo de arquitectos americanos en la Base Ramey de Aguadilla con quienes trabajó como arquitecto. En 1946 comenzó a trabajar en área de Ingeniería y Arquitectura de la Autoridad de Hogares en San Juan, hoy conocida como CRUV. Allí se desarrolló en el área de ingeniería, arquitectura, planificación de hogares, eliminación de arrabales, remodelación de caseríos y viviendas. En 1958 comenzó a diseñar residencias privadas y comerciales. Estableció su propia compañía de construcción con la que se dedicó a realizar obras de construcción de escuelas y centros gubernamentales en Carolina, San Lorenzo, Río Piedras, Camuy y Hatillo.
museocoleccion.uprrp.edu/people/726/mig…
Miguel A. Soto Cuevas (Lares, PR 1918-2010)
Architect, Musician and Graphic Artist. He began his university studies in Agronomy at the College of Agriculture and Mechanical Arts of Mayagüez; known today as the Mayagüez Campus, U.P.R. He sang in the choir and organized a quartet where he was the singer. He also traveled around towns and colleges of the Island promoting the Colegio. Later, he moved to the United States, where in 1941 he obtained a Bachelor’s Degree in Industrial Education with a concentration in Architecture from Texas A&M University, College Station, Texas. Upon returning to Puerto Rico, he worked as a teacher for a year in Aguadilla. He then joined a group of American architects at the Ramey Base in Aguadilla with whom he worked as an architect. In 1946 he began working in the area of Engineering and Architecture of the Homes Authority in San Juan, today known as CRUV. There he worked in the areas of engineering, architecture, home planning, elimination of slums, remodeling of farmhouses and homes. In 1958 he began designing private and commercial residences. He established his own construction company with which he dedicated himself to the construction of schools and government centers in Carolina, San Lorenzo, Río Piedras, Camuy and Hatillo.

Jorge “Rito” Cordero Ramos
 (Hatillo, PR, 1982).

In the same year he is part of a selection of ten students who travel to the art fair, ARCO in Madrid.

Gabriela Zanandrea,
 (Buenos Aires, Argentina, 1965)
Estudió dibujo y pintura en Buenos Aires y Madrid. 
Entre los años 2002 y 2008 residió en Puerto Rico y completó sus estudios en Artes Plásticas en la Universidad de Puerto Rico. Durante este periodo trabajó en los talleres del grabador Martin García Rivera. Además de dedicarse a las artes plásticas, trabajó en arte para cine, publicidad y televisión; y en escenografía para teatro. Expone colectiva e individualmente desde 1996 en Argentina, en los Estados y Puerto Rico. Sus obras componen colecciones privadas y públicas en Argentina, Inglaterra, Malasia, Estados Unidos, Puerto Rico y España. Vive y trabaja en Salta, Argentina desde 2008.
Gabriela Zanandrea, (Buenos Aires, Argentina, 1965)
She studied drawing and painting in Buenos Aires and Madrid. Between 2002 and 2008 she lived in Puerto Rico and completed her studies in Plastic Arts at the University of Puerto Rico. During this period, she worked in the workshops of engraver Martin García Rivera. In addition to the visual arts, she worked in art for film, advertising and television; and in scenography for theater. She has exhibited collectively and individually since 1996 in Argentina, the United States and Puerto Rico. Her works are part of private and public collections in Argentina, England, Malaysia, United States, Puerto Rico and Spain. Lives and works in Salta, Argentina since 2008.

inventory.name: Julio Rosado Del Valle – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Julio Rosado Del Valle
 (Cataño, PR, 1922- San Juan, PR, 2009)
Pintor, dibujante, artista, diseñador gráfico e ilustrador. Se inició en el mundo del arte en el taller de Facundo Figueroa y prosiguió con el pintor español Cristóbal Ruíz en la Universidad de Puerto Rico. En 1946, becado por la Universidad de Puerto Rico, estudió en New School for Social Research de Nueva York. Allí fue discípulo del pintor cubano Mario Carreño y del muralista ecuatoriano Camilo Egas. En 1947 recibió una beca para estudiar en la Academia de Bellas Artes de Florencia y viajó también a París. Fue cofundador del Centro de Arte Puertorriqueño en San Juan en 1950. De regreso a Puerto Rico se desempeñó como diseñador e ilustrador de libros para la División de Educación a la Comunidad y el Departamento de Instrucción Pública en San Juan. Fue artista residente de la Universidad de Puerto Rico. En 1957 obtuvo medalla de oro en el certamen Mural Paintings Exhibition, de The Architectural League en Nueva York y la beca de la Fundación Guggenheim, en Nueva York. Sus obras fluctúan entre la figuración y la abstracción, lo que refleja su búsqueda constante de una expresión artística propia.
Julio Rosado Del Valle
 (Cataño, PR, 1922- San Juan, PR, 2009)
Painter, draftsman, graphic artist and designer, and illustrator. His first steps in the art world were at the Facundo Figueroa workshop and later with Spanish painter Cristóbal Ruiz at the University of Puerto Rico. In 1946, on a scholarship from the University of Puerto Rico, he studied at the New School for Social Research in New York under Cuban painter Mario Carreño and Ecuadorian muralist Camilo Egas. In 1947, he received a scholarship to study at the Fine Arts Academy in Florence and also traveled to Paris. He was co-founder of the Center for Puerto Rican Art in San Juan in 1950. Upon his return to Puerto Rico, he worked as a book designer and illustrator for the Community Education Division of the Public Education Department in San Juan. He was resident artist at the University of Puerto Rico. In 1957, he won a gold medal at the Mural Paintings Exhibition of the Architectural League in New York and a scholarship from the Guggenheim Foundation in New York. His works fluctuate between the figurative and the abstract, reflecting his constant search for a personal artistic expression.

inventory.name: Residencia Reyes Veray – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Residencia Reyes Veray, Guaynabo – 1982
DESCRIPCIÓN 
1. Fecha de Terminación: Mayo de 1982
2. Localización: Urb. Parkville 
Guaynabo, Puerto Rico
3. Uso de la estructura: Residencia
4. Descripción del programa:
Aumentar un modelo de casa básica de urbanización para añadir todos los 
requerimientos de espacio y maximizar la utilización del solar.
Transformar una residencia total dependiente de la energía eléctrica, carente de luz y 
ventilación, a un ambiente natural, fresco, ventilado y tropical, explorando el recurso 
clima.
5. Materiales y tipo de construcción:
Madera y Hormigón
6. Costo: $ 42 mil
Ampliación de la residencia de 20 años del cliente donde existía una gran fijación emocional de su primera y única casa. Añadir las nuevas áreas requeridas aprovechando el máximo de la casa básica e integrando los elementos de continuidad: el mural escultórico original de la fachada, la casita de juego de los niños cuando pequeños, el gran árbol de cupey frente a la casa.
Tropicalizar el ambiente aprovechando todos los recursos posibles:
Aislante en los techos, ventiladores de gravedad, ventilación cruzada, ventanales, vitrales, claraboyas, celdas solares, transmisión de luz y aire utilizando paredes deslizantes, y el uso de la ventilación para proteger del sol y canalizar las brisas. 
Integrar la expresión exterior al contexto urbano del vecindario con una solución sencilla y discreta.

inventory.description:
Reynaldo González Bravo
 (Arecibo, PR, 1968)
Pintor. Comenzó sus estudios formales en arte en 1992. Posee un Bachillerato en Artes Plásticas con concentración en Artes Gráficas de la Escuela de Artes Plásticas de San Juan. Hizo su Maestría en Artes Plásticas de la Universidad Interamericana de Puerto Rico, Recinto de San Germán. Su trabajo se ha presentado en diversos certámenes y exposiciones. En el 2000 ganó el Primer Premio en Pintura del Certamen de Arte Joven de la Corporación de Puerto Rico para el Nuevo Milenio. También ha sido premiado en La Habana, Cuba con el Primer Premio de Mejor Ilustración y la Fundación Alfonso Arana por Mejor Dibujo.
Reynaldo González Bravo
 (Arecibo, PR, 1968)
Painter. He began his formal studies in art in 1992. He has a Bachelor’s Degree in Fine Arts with a concentration in Graphic Arts from the Escuela de Artes Plásticas de San Juan. She received her Master’s Degree in Fine Arts from the Interamerican University of Puerto Rico, San Germán Campus. His work has been presented in various competitions and exhibitions. In 2000 he won the First Prize in Painting at the Young Art Contest of the Puerto Rico Corporation for the New Millennium. He has also been awarded in Havana, Cuba with the First Prize for Best Illustration and the Alfonso Arana Foundation for Best Drawing.

inventory.name: Antonio Maldonado – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Antonio Maldonado
 (Manatí, P.R., 1920 – San Juan, P.R., 2006)
Pintor, grabador y cartelista. Realizo sus estudios en la Escuela Nacional de Artes Plásticas de México y tomo cursos con el pintor Español Cristóbal Ruiz en la Universidad de Puerto Rico. Trabajo en el taller del pintor Juan Rosado del Valle en Puerta de Puerta de Tierra, San Juan en donde conoció a Rafael Tufiño. Trabajo en la División de Educación de la Comunidad desde los años 50 y desde 1963 dirigió el Taller de Grafica. Creo junto a Tufiño el ‘Atelier’, lugar que por diez años sirvió de estimulo para los artistas jóvenes. Su obra es un acercamiento a la realidad cultural cotidiana en que los personajes de esta cotidianidad son parte de sus obras.
Antonio Maldonado
 (Manatí, P.R., 1920 – San Juan, P.R., 2006)
Painter, engraver and poster artist. He studied at the Escuela Nacional de Artes Plásticas in Mexico and took courses with Spanish painter Cristóbal Ruiz at the University of Puerto Rico. He worked in the workshop of painter Juan Rosado del Valle in Puerta de Puerta de Tierra, San Juan where he met Rafael Tufiño. He worked in the Community Education Division since the 50’s and since 1963 he directed the Graphic Workshop. Together with Tufiño, he created the ‘Atelier’, a place that for ten years served as a stimulus for young artists. His work is an approach to the everyday cultural reality in which the characters of this everyday life are part of his works.

inventory.name: Héctor Rafael Rodríguez – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Héctor Rafael Rodríguez
 (Santiago de Compostela, España, 1973)
Pintor, dibujante y educador. A los tres años de edad regresó con su familia a Puerto Rico. Completó su Bachillerato en Bellas Artes con concentración en Pintura en el Colegio de Artes Plásticas de la Universidad de Syracuse. En 1996 se trasladó a la ciudad de Nueva York, donde trabajó como catalogador y manejador de arte para varios departamentos de arte de la casa de subastas Christie’s New York (Departamento de Arte Latinoameriano, Pintura europea del siglo diecinueve, Departamento de Arte y objetos marítimos). Durante este periodo, tuvo la oportunidad de estudiar con detenimiento el trabajo de algunos de los artistas de mayor relevancia en la historia del arte, además de estar en contacto con sus trabajos. Su obra ha sido expuesta en Puerto Rico, Italia, Nueva York y Massachusetts.
Héctor Rafael Rodríguez
 (Santiago de Compostela, España, 1973)
Painter, draftsman, and educator. He returned to Puerto Rico with his family at the age of three. He completed his Bachelor of Fine Arts with a major in Painting at the School of Visual Arts at Syracuse University. In 1996, he moved to New York City, where he worked as art cataloger and manager for several art departments at Christie’s New York (Department of Latin American Art, Nineteenth Century European Painting, Department of Art and Marine Objects). During this period, he was able to study in detail the work of some of the most relevant artists the history of art, in addition to coming into contact with their work. His work has been exhibited in Puerto Rico, Italy, New York, and Massachusetts.

inventory.name: Juan Bautista Climént – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Juan Bautista Climént
 (Ithaca, NY, 1989)
Nace en la ciudad de Ithaca, Nueva York, en 1989, pero se cría en la Ciudad de México. Abandona sus estudios de cine animado en México para irse a vivir al Caribe, a la tierra natal de su madre, Puerto Rico, donde estudia pintura en la Escuela de Artes Plásticas de Puerto Rico (EAP) en el Viejo San Juan. Su trabajo, aunque abarca diversos medios, proyecta reflexiones siempre de carácter dibujístico. Ha mostrado su obra en numerosas exposiciones individuales y colectivas en Puerto Rico y México. A comienzos del año 2013, gesta la Escuela Pública, Libre y Gratuita de Dibujo, un espacio pedagógico y de diálogo en torno al dibujo con toda persona, sea cual sea su profesión. Fue Director de Área, Lugar de Proyectos, en Caguas, Puerto Rico.
Juan Bautista Climént
 (Ithaca, NY, 1989)
Born in Ithaca, New York, in 1989, but grew up in Mexico City. He abandoned his animated film studies in Mexico to move to the Caribbean, to his mother’s homeland of Puerto Rico, where he studied painting at the Escuela de Artes Plásticas de Puerto Rico (EAP) in Old San Juan. His work, although it encompasses diverse media, always projects reflections of a draftsmanlike nature. He has shown his work in numerous solo and group exhibitions in Puerto Rico and Mexico. At the beginning of 2013, he created the Escuela Pública, Libre y Gratuita de Dibujo, a pedagogical space for dialogue about drawing with everyone, regardless of their profession. He was Director of Area, Lugar de Proyectos, in Caguas, Puerto Rico.

Arleen Casanova Ferrer
 (Luquillo, PR, 1967-2013)
Grabadora. Completó un Bachillerato en Arte en la Escuela de Artes Plásticas de Puerto Rico. En 1993 presentó la muestra individual “Lo vivido y lo grabado” en la Galería Coabey en San Juan. Posteriormente, en 1995 presentó “Xilo-cofre de la identidad” en la Galería San Juan Conservation Studio en el Viejo San Juan y en 1998 “El regreso” en Vintage Art Gallery en Santurce. Ha exhibido colectivamente en Puerto Rico, México e Italia.
Arleen Casanova Ferrer
 (Luquillo, PR, 1967-2013)
Engraver. She completed a Bachelor’s Degree in Art at the Escuela de Artes Plásticas de Puerto Rico. In 1993 she presented the solo exhibition “Lo vivido y lo grabado” at the Coabey Gallery in San Juan. Subsequently, in 1995 she presented “Xilo-cofre de la identidad” at the San Juan Conservation Studio Gallery in Old San Juan and in 1998 “El regreso” at Vintage Art Gallery in Santurce. inventory.name: Jean Michel Fiedler – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Jean Michel Fiedler
 (San Juan, P.R., 1967)
Pintor y dibujante. En 1986 estudia en Pratt Institue de Nueva York, luego en 1987 en la Universidad de Puerto Rico y finalmente en University of the Art en Pennsylvania. Ha sido profesor en la Liga de Estudiantes de Arte de San Juan, la Universidad del Sagrado Corazón y la Escuela de Artes Plásticas de San Juan. Se ha desempeñado como ilustrador de San Juan City Publications y The San Juan Star. Ha hecho murales, mosaicos, pinturas escenográficas decorativas, ilustraciones y diseños para productos de marcas reconocidas. Se le han otorgado premios entre los que se encuentran: Honor, en Print Magazine 29th Annual International Cover Desing Competition en Nueva York; William H. Ely Award for Excelence in Illustration en Pennsylvania y The Harriet P. Hughes Award for Best Pen and Ink Illustration en Filadelfia. Su obra se ha expuesto en Puerto Rico y Estados Unidos.
Jean Michel Fiedler
 (San Juan, P.R., 1967)
Painter and draftsman. In 1986 he studied at the Pratt Institute in New York, in 1987 at the University of Puerto Rico, and finally at the Art University in Pennsylvania. He has been a professor at the San Juan League of Art Students, at Sacred Heart University, and at the School of Visual Arts in San Juan. He has worked as an illustrator for San Juan City Publications and The San Juan Star. He has created murals, mosaics, decorative scenery paintings, illustrations, and designs for well-known brand products. Among the awards he has received are: Honor, in the Print Magazine 29th Annual International Cover Design Competition in New York, the William H. Ely Award for Excellence in Illustration in Pennsylvania, and The Harriet P. Hughes Award for Best Pen and Ink Illustration in Philadelphia. His work has been displayed in Puerto Rico and the United States.

inventory.name: Bernardo Hogan – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Bernardo Hogan
 (Argentina, 1921 – Puerto Rico, 2020)
Ceramista. Artista autodidacta. Llegó a Puerto Rico en 1968. En 1980 fundó junto a otros ceramistas, incluyendo a su esposa la artista Susana Espinosa, la Casa Candina. Trabajó en el taller de cerámica de la Liga de Estudiantes de Arte de San Juan. Recibió la medalla de oro en Concurso Internacional de la Cerámica en Faenza donde también exhibió. En el 2017 se presentó la exhibición Bernardo Hogan: una retrospectiva en el Museo de Arte e Historia de San Juan. Su obra se encuentra en importantes colecciones en Puerto Rico e Italia.
Bernardo Hogan
 (Argentina, 1921 – Puerto Rico, 2020)
Ceramist. Self-taught artist. He arrived in Puerto Rico in 1968. In 1980 he founded Casa Candina with other ceramists, including his wife, artist Susana Espinosa. Worked in the ceramics workshop of the Art Students League of San Juan. He received the gold medal in International Ceramics Competition in Faenza where he also exhibited. In 2017, the exhibition Bernardo Hogan: a retrospective was presented at the San Juan Museum of Art and History. His work is in important collections in Puerto Rico and Italy.

Antonio Montes de Oca,
 (Carora, Venezuela, 1968)
Estudia en la Escuela de Artes Plásticas “Martín Tovar y Tovar ” de Barquisimeto. Es uno de los jóvenes valores de la plástica larense. Su obra alejada de la figuración tradicional, responde a una manera distinta de aproximación a la realidad de la naturaleza y de los objetos domésticos. En la década de los ochenta, en sus inicios, Montes de Oca abordó el paisaje, apegándose a la escuela tradicionalista de Lara. Luego fue abordando la naturaleza y los objetos de una forma simple y diáfana, con toda la plasticidad posible dándole a a sus motivos un cierto dejo de infantil o elemental. Ahora Montes de Oca ha hecho mucho más rica su pintura, más actualizada, más contemporánea, se ha convertido en un artista sobrio, disciplinado y comedido.
Antonio Montes de Oca, (Carora, Venezuela, 1968)
He studied at the School of Plastic Arts “Martín Tovar y Tovar” in Barquisimeto. He is one of the young values of the larense plastic arts. His work, far from traditional figuration, responds to a different way of approaching the reality of nature and domestic objects. In the eighties, in his beginnings, Montes de Oca approached the landscape, sticking to the traditionalist school of Lara. Then he approached nature and objects in a simple and diaphanous way, with all the plasticity possible, giving his motifs a certain childish or elemental touch. Now Montes de Oca has made his painting much richer, more updated, more contemporary, he has become a sober, disciplined and restrained artist.

inventory.description:

 (San Juan, PR, 1973)
En 1997 completa un Bachillerato en Artes Plásticas de la Escuela de Artes Plásticas de Puerto Rico. Posteriormente completa una Maestría en Arte en la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México. Su obra ha sido expuesta colectivamente en Puerto Rico, Estados Unidos, México, Nicaragua, Francia y Cuba.

inventory.name: María Luisa Penne de Castillo – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
María Luisa Penne de Castillo, (Ponce, PR 1913 – San Juan, PR, 2005)
Pintora, grabadora y educadora. Comenzó sus estudios formales en arte en el Instituto Pratt en Nueva York de 1932 a 1935. Obtuvo su BA en la Universidad de Puerto Rico en 1939 y su MA en Artes en el Art Institute de Chicago en 1947. Realizó Estudios doctorales en la Universidad de Columbia de Nueva York entre 1940 a 1961. Fue Directora del Departamento de Bellas Artes del Instituto Politécnico de San Germán de 1940 a 1961 y Profesora de la Universidad de Puerto Rico en Mayagüez de 1961 a 1980.
Sus exposiciones individuales incluyen: Pinturas y Artes Aplicadas de María Luisa P. de Castillo en la Universidad de Puerto Rico en 1948; Cuadros para el hogar: Acuarelas de María Luisa P. de Castillo en el Hotel Condado en 1952; Exposición de acuarelas de María Luisa P. De Castillo en el Colegio de Agricultura y Artes Mecánicas de Mayaguez en 1961; Retrospectiva de María Luisa P. de Castillo en el Departamento de Instrucción Pública en 1972; Exposición Homenaje a María Luisa Castillo en la Universidad Interamericana, Recinto de San Germán en 1979; Exposición Homenaje en el Ateneo Puertorriqueño en 1985 y Exposición Retrospectiva: María Luisa Penne de Castillo en Museo Casa Roig, UPR Humacao en 1998. Una selección de sus exhibiciones colectivas incluyen: Primera Exposición Arte Independiente de Puerto Rico en la UPR en 1939, Liga de Artistas Americanos en el Ateneo Puertorriqueño en 1945; El paisaje de Puerto Rico, en el ICP en 1961; Museo de Arte de Ponce en 1968; IV Bienal de San Juan del Grabado Latinoamericano en 1979; Exposición Colectiva de Mujeres Artistas dedicada a la Prof. María Luisa Castillo en La Fortaleza, S.J. en 1979; Pintura y gráfica de los años 50 en el ICP en 1985; Mujeres Artistas de Puerto Rico en el Museo de Bellas Artes del ICP en1986; De Oller a los Cuarenta: La pintura en Puerto Rico 1898–1948 en el Museo de Historia, Antropología y Arte de la Universidad de Puerto Rico en 1988; Mujeres Artistas: Protagonistas de los ochenta en el Museo de Arte Contemporáneo en 1990 y Los tesoros de la pintura puertorriqueña en el Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico en 2000.
María Luisa Penne de Castillo, (Ponce, PR 1913 – San Juan, PR, 2005)
Painter, printmaker and educator. She began her formal studies in art at Pratt Institute in New York from 1932 to 1935. She received her BA from the University of Puerto Rico in 1939 and her MA in Art from the Art Institute of Chicago in 1947. She did doctoral studies at Columbia University in New York from 1940 to 1961. She was Director of the Fine Arts Department at the Polytechnic Institute of San Germán from 1940 to 1961 and Professor at the University of Puerto Rico in Mayagüez from 1961 to 1980.
Her solo exhibitions include: Paintings and Applied Arts by María Luisa P. de Castillo at the University of Puerto Rico in 1948; Pictures for the Home: Watercolors by María Luisa P. de Castillo at the Condado Hotel in 1952; Exhibition of watercolors by María Luisa P. De Castillo at the College of Agriculture and Mechanical Arts in Mayaguez in 1961; Retrospective of María Luisa P. de Castillo at the Department of Public Instruction in 1972; Homage Exhibition to María Luisa Castillo at the Interamerican University, San Germán Campus in 1979; Homage Exhibition at the Puerto Rican Athenaeum in 1985 and Retrospective Exhibition: María Luisa Penne de Castillo at Museo Casa Roig, UPR Humacao in 1998. A selection of her group exhibitions include: First Exhibition of Independent Art of Puerto Rico at the UPR in 1939, League of American Artists at the Ateneo Puertorriqueño in 1945; The Landscape of Puerto Rico, at the ICP in 1961; Museo de Arte de Ponce in 1968; IV Biennial of San Juan of Latin American Engraving in 1979; Collective Exhibition of Women Artists dedicated to Prof. María Luisa Castillo at La Fortaleza in 1985 and Retrospective Exhibition: María Luisa Penne Castillo at Museo Casa Roig, UPR Humacao in 1998. María Luisa Castillo at La Fortaleza, S.J. in 1979; Painting and Graphics of the 1950s at the ICP in 1985; Women Artists of Puerto Rico at the Museo de Bellas Artes of the ICP in 1986; From Oller to the Forties: Painting in Puerto Rico 1898-1948 at the Museo de Historia, Antropología y Arte of the University of Puerto Rico in 1988; Mujeres Artistas: Protagonistas de los ochenta at the Museo de Arte Contemporáneo in 1990 and Los tesoros de la pintura puertorriqueña at the Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico in 2000.

inventory.name: Nayda Collazo Lloréns – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Nayda Collazo Lloréns
 (San Juan, P.R., 1968)
Pintora, grabadora, video-artista y creadora de instalaciones. Completó en 1990 un Bachillerato en Bellas Artes con concentración en Grabado de Massachussets College of Art y en el 2002, una Maestría en Artes Plásticas de New York University; donde además se le concedió el Premio Jack Goodman de arte y tecnología. Ha realizado varias residencias artísticas, como en la isla de Skópelos en Grecia y el programa de Harvestworks en Nueva York. Ha presentado más de una decena de exposiciones individuales y ha participado en sobre treinta exposiciones colectivas a nivel internacional. Ha recibido gran cantidad de premios y distinciones de entidades culturales en Puerto Rico y Estados Unidos, entre las cuales se encuentran el Ateneo Puertorriqueño, el Museo de Arte de Ponce y Massachussets College. Actualmente trabaja y reside en Nueva York. Trabaja con los conceptos del tiempo y la memoria utilizando símbolos, repetición de imágenes y números.
Nayda Collazo Lloréns
 (San Juan, P.R., 1968)
Painter, printmaker, video artist and creator of installations. She completed in 1990 a Bachelor of Fine Arts with a concentration in Printmaking from Massachusetts College of Art and in 2002, a Master of Fine Arts from New York University; where she was also awarded the Jack Goodman Prize for art and technology. She has completed several artist residencies, such as on the island of Skopelos in Greece and the Harvestworks program in New York. She has presented more than a dozen solo exhibitions and has participated in over thirty group exhibitions internationally. She has received numerous awards and distinctions from cultural entities in Puerto Rico and the United States, including the Ateneo Puertorriqueño, the Museo de Arte de Ponce and Massachusetts College. She currently works and resides in New York. She works with the concepts of time and memory using symbols, repetition of images and numbers.

Jonathan Gardner
 (Lexington, KY, EEUU, 1982)
Jonathan Gardner started his art studies at the Polymoda Technical in Florence, Italy, then completed a BFA in the School of Visual Arts of New York, coursed a Post Baccalaureate Studio Certificate in the Art Institute of Chicago and later completed an MFA in that same institution. His work has been exhibited all over the United States and other countries such as Germany and Spain. He currently lives and works in New York City.

inventory.description:
Ivonne María Marcial
Fotográfa y arquitecta. Completó estudios de Maestría en la Escuela de Arquitectura de la Universidad de Puerto Rico. Se trasladó a Bélgica donde estudió fotografía de arte en el “Institut-Saint Luc” en la ciudad de Lieja. Entre sus premios y becas están el Concurso “Saving the Light” de En Foco, Inc., New York (1996) y la Beca del Fondo Permanente para las Artes, San Juan, PR (1995). Actualmente es profesora de diseño arquitectónico, dibujo y fotografía en la Nueva Escuela de Arquitectura de la Universidad Politécnica.
Ivonne María Marcial
Photographer and architect. She completed her Master’s degree at the School of Architecture of the University of Puerto Rico. She moved to Belgium where she studied art photography at the “Institut-Saint Luc” in the city of Liege. Among her awards and grants are the “Saving the Light” Competition of En Foco, Inc. in New York (1996) and the Permanent Fund for the Arts Grant, San Juan, PR (1995). She currently teaches architectural design, drawing and photography at the New School of Architecture, Polytechnic University.

inventory.name: Luis Ivorra – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Luis Ivorra
 (Mallorca, España, 1952)
Pintor y escultor. En 1978 se trasladó a Puerto Rico donde obtuvo un Bachillerato de la Universidad Interamericana, San Juan, Puerto Rico. Realizó estudios libres en la Escuela de Artes Plásticas y la Liga de Arte de San Juan. Participó en diferentes clases y talleres de escultura, dibujo y pintura bajo la tutela de Domingo García, Betsy Padín, Jerry Saint Germain y Arnaldo Roche Rabell. Actualmente es profesor de cerámica en la Liga de Arte de San Juan. En el 1999 recibe el Primer Premio de Adquisición de Casa Candina en la VI Bienal de Cerámica Contemporánea en San Juan, Puerto Rico. Ha exhibido en Puerto Rico y Estados Unidos tanto individual como colectivamente. En el 2007 participó de la VI Bienal Internacional de Arte Contemporáneo en Firenze, Italia.
Luis Ivorra
 (Mallorca, Spain, 1952)
Painter and sculptor. In 1978 he moved to Puerto Rico where he obtained a Bachelor’s degree from the Universidad Interamericana, San Juan, Puerto Rico. He studied at the Escuela de Artes Plásticas and the Liga de Arte de San Juan. He participated in different classes and workshops of sculpture, drawing and painting under the tutelage of Domingo García, Betsy Padín, Jerry Saint Germain and Arnaldo Roche Rabell. He currently teaches ceramics at the Art League of San Juan. In 1999 he received the First Prize of Acquisition of Casa Candina in the VI Biennial of Contemporary Ceramics in San Juan, Puerto Rico. He has exhibited in Puerto Rico and the United States both individually and collectively. In 2007 he participated in the VI International Biennial of Contemporary Art in Florence, Italy.

inventory.name: David Sepúlveda – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
David Sepúlveda (Rimx)
 (Bayamón, Puerto Rico, 1981)
David received his diploma from the Central High School of Visual Arts in Santurce, PR where he studied drawing, painting, etching, sculpture, and xylography and began his interest in urban art. Later, he continued studying at the School of Visual Arts in Old San Juan, PR, where he specialized in drawing the human figure, portrait and figurative art. He also studied editorial illustration, xylography, engraving and graphic design. After finishing his studies, he dedicated himself to incorporating the various techniques of classic art into urban art, specializing in murals. He has also worked doing editorial illustrations for magazines, newspapers, children’s publications, book covers, etc. David is a member of the artist collective CORO, which is comprised of graphic designers, illustrators and visual artists. The CORO has successfully exhibited in Puerto Rico, Tokyo, Paris and New York. In addition to his collaborative works, David has held many solo exhibits. He also curated the Espacio Disponible show for the Caribbean University in Bayamón, PR.

inventory.name: Jorge Luis Pardo Rosado – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Jorge Pardo Rosado
 (San Juan, PR, 1970)
Pintor. Completó un Bachillerato en Artes de la Universidad de Puerto Rico y una Maestría en Artes Visuales de la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México. Su obra fue premiada en la Tercera Bienal de Arte Joven, Hato Rey, Puerto Rico. Exhibe en Puerto Rico, México y Estados Unidos. Su obra se caracteriza por la exploración del espacio en texturas que logra con trazos gestuales, múltiples y sobrepuestos. Es una obra compleja, lograda con el mínimo de elementos, el uso de la mancha lineal y pigmentos monocromos.
Jorge Pardo Rosado (San Juan, PR, 1970)
Painter. He completed a Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of Puerto Rico and a Master’s degree in Visual Arts from the Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México. His work was awarded in the Third Biennial of Young Art, Hato Rey, Puerto Rico. He exhibits in Puerto Rico, Mexico and the United States. His work is characterized by the exploration of space in textures that he achieves with gestural, multiple and superimposed strokes. It is a complex work, achieved with the minimum of elements, the use of the linear stain and monochrome pigments.

inventory.name: Carlos Santiago – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Carlos Santiago
 (Peñuelas, PR, 1978)
Pintor. Egresado de la Escuela de Artes Plásticas de Puerto Rico en el 2001, año en que recibió la Beca Arana, la cual le permitió un año de residencia en París. Durante su estancia tomó clases en la institución Teophile Gautier, en el Taller de Bellas Artes de la Marie y en el Estudio de Daniel Fisher; además de trabajar en su taller en Gambetta y en el de Alfonso Arana. Ingresó también al grupo de “Les Rats Du Champs”, quienes viajan anualmente a Los Alpes para pintar sólo con acuarelas. Ha tenido varias exhibiciones individuales en y fuera de Puerto Rico. Colectivamente ha participado en exhibiciones en Estados Unidos, Canadá, Francia, Perú y Puerto Rico. En el 2004 participó en la Casa de la UNESCO en República Dominicana. Con su expresionismo nos habla de la resistencia, del humanismo y el desafío.
Carlos Santiago
 (Peñuelas, PR, 1978)
Painter. He graduated from the Puerto Rico School of Visual Arts in 2001 and was awarded the Arana Scholarship, which allowed him to live in Paris for a year. During his stay, he took classes at the Teophile Gautier institute, the De la Marie Fine Arts Workshop, and the Daniel Fisher Studio, in addition to working at the Alfonso Arana atelier and at his own atelier in Gambetta. He also joined the “Les Rats Du Champs” group, who travel yearly to the Alps to paint exclusively in watercolors. He has held several individual exhibitions in Puerto Rico and abroad. He has participated in collective exhibitions the United States, Canada, France, Peru, and Puerto Rico. In 2004 he participated in the UNESCO House in the Dominican Republic. His expressionism speaks to us of resistance, humanism, and defiance.

inventory.name: Miguel Pou Becerra – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Miguel Pou Becerra
 (Ponce, PR, 1880-San Juan, PR, 1968)
Pintor, dibujante y profesor. Se inició en el dibujo con Pedro Clausells y en la pintura con el español Santiago Meana. Luego de obtener un Bachillerato en Artes del Instituto Provincial de Puerto Rico, trabajó como maestro del Departamento de Instrucción. En 1910 fundó en Ponce la Academia Miguel Pou, una escuela de arte que estimuló a numerosos jóvenes a interesarse por el arte. En 1919 viajó a Nueva York para estudiar en la Liga de Estudiantes de Arte y en 1935 a Filadelfia para estudiar en la Academia de Bellas Artes. Su obra ha sido reconocida en Puerto Rico, Estados Unidos y París. Entre sus discípulos se encuentran Olga Albizu, Horacio Castaing, Rafael Ríos Rey y Luis Quero Chiesa. En el 2006 el Museo de Arte de Ponce organizó una exhibición que viajó al prestigioso Worcester Art Museum de Massachussets y que incluyó obras suyas, de José Campeche y Francisco Oller. Su pintura refleja la influencia impresionista en la importancia que le otorga a la luz y al color. Se inspiró en el paisaje rural y urbano, en los tipos populares y en la figura humana.
Miguel Pou Becerra
 (Ponce, PR, 1880-San Juan, PR, 1968)
Painter, draftsman, and professor. He began drawing with Pedro Clausells and painting with Spaniard Santiago Meana. After receiving a Bachelor of Arts from the Provincial Institute of Puerto Rico, he worked as a teacher with the Department of Education. In 1910 he established the Miguel Pou Academy in Ponce, an art school that stimulated numerous youngsters to develop an interest in art. In 1919 he traveled to New York to study at the League of Art Students, and in 1935 to Philadelphia to study at the Academy of Fine Arts. His work has been recognized in Puerto Rico, the United States, and Paris. Among his disciples are Olga Albizu, Horacio Castaign, Rafael Ríos Rey, and Luis Quero Chiesa. In 2006 the Ponce Art Museum organized an exhibit of his work and that of José Campeche and Francisco Oller, which traveled to the prestigious Worcester Art Museum in Massachusetts. The importance he places on light and color in his paintings reflects the influence of impressionism. He was inspired by the rural and urban landscapes, popular characters, and the human figure.

inventory.name: Arnaldo Roche Rabell – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Arnaldo Roche Rabell
 (San Juan, PR, 1955 – San Juan, PR, 2018)
Pintor. Comenzó su formación en la Escuela de Arte Luchetti en Santurce, donde tuvo como maestro a Lope Max Díaz. En 1969 estudió en la Escuela de Arquitectura de la Universidad de Puerto Rico y continuó en Art Institute de Chicago, donde obtuvo su Bachillerato y su Maestría en Bellas Artes en 1984. Desde entonces se ha dedicado por completo a la pintura. Es uno de los artistas puertorriqueños contemporáneos más destacados en la plástica nacional e internacional. Su obra pictórica ha sido expuesta en diversos países como México, Brasil, Venezuela, España y Ecuador, entre otros. Ha participado en numerosos eventos internacionales, ganando gran cantidad de premios y distinciones. Su obra de intenso contenido psicológico explora el autorretrato, figuras familiares y el paisaje, en obras de gran formato, en las cuales el color y las múltiples texturas son el fundamento de su propuesta fuertemente expresiva.
Arnaldo Roche Rabell
 (San Juan, PR, 1955 – 2018)
Painter. He began his studies at the Luchetti Art School in Santurce, where he studied under Lope Max Díaz. In 1969, he began studies at the University of Puerto Rico School of Architecture and continued at the Chicago Art Institute, from where he received his Bachelor’s degree and Master of Fine Arts in 1984. Since then he has devoted himself entirely to painting. He is one of the most outstanding contemporary Puerto Rican artists in national and international visual arts. His work has been exhibited in numerous countries, such as Mexico, Brazil, Venezuela, Spain, and Ecuador, among others. He has participated in many international events and has received various prizes and distinctions. Color and multiple textures are the foundation of his strongly expressive large format work, which has an intensely psychological content and includes self-portraits, familiar figures, and landscapes.

Uziel Orlandi
 (San Juan, PR, 1988)
En 2009 ingresó a la Universidad de Puerto Rico a cursar estudios en artes gráficas con especialización en grabado. Ha participado de exposiciones colectivas tales como Las Jornadas del Grabado, La máscara, Malas impresiones y TYPO. Uziel Orlandi (San Juan, PR, 1988)
In 2009 he entered the University of Puerto Rico to study graphic arts with a specialization in printmaking. In 2014 the Colectivo Camiseta (CoCa), of which he is co-creator, presented El Galerinto, an exhibition composed of interactive installations, works and murals, as part of Santurce es Ley 5. He has participated in group exhibitions such as Las Jornadas del Grabado, La máscara, Malas impresiones and TYPO. He has painted in collective murals as part of events such as the Feria de Cultura Urbana, Los Muros Hablan and Santurce es Ley. His work has been recognized in Caribbean: Together Appart / Contemporary Artists from (part of) the Carribean and in the International Biennial of Printmaking in Varna, Bulgaria. inventory.name: Jaime Carrero – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Jaime Carrero
 (Mayagüez, P.R., 1931 – San Germán, P.R., 2013)
Pintor, dibujante, novelista, dramaturgo y poeta. En 1949 estudió en el Art Institute Center de Nueva York. En 1956 obtuvo su Bachillerato en Artes en la Universidad Interamericana de Puerto Rico y completó una Maestría en Artes en Pratt Institute de Nueva York en 1957. Tomó cursos avanzados de pintura en Florencia, en 1961 y al año siguiente, de historia del arte en Columbia University, en Nueva York y en el 1976, en Yale University. Ha sido profesor del Departamento de Arte en la Universidad Interamericana de Puerto Rico, en San Germán, donde además fungió como director de 1979 a 1995. Además de ser reconocido como pintor, ha sido premiado por sus aportaciones a la literatura en los géneros de cuento, teatro, poesía, novela y crítica de arte. En 1966 y 1967 recibió premios del Ateneo Puertorriqueño por drama, novela y cuento. Su obra se ha presentado en más de cuarenta exhibiciones colectivas en y fuera de Puerto Rico. Su obra expresa sarcásticamente una temática social y política.
Jaime Carrero
 (Mayagüez, PR, 1931 – San Germán, PR, 2013)
Painter, draftsman, novelist, playwright, and poet. In 1949 he studied at the Art Institute Center in New York. In 1956 he earned his Bachelor of Arts at the Inter American University of Puerto Rico, and in 1957 he completed his Master of Arts at the Pratt Institute in New York. He studied advanced painting courses in Florence in 1961, and the following year he took art history courses at Columbia University in New York. He has been a professor at the Art Department of Inter American University of Puerto Rico in San Germán, and was its director from 1979 to 1995. In addition to his recognition as a painter, he has received awards for his literary work in novels, short stories, plays, poetry, and art criticism. In 1966 and 1967 he received awards from the Ateneo Puertorriqueño for drama, novel, and short story. His works have appeared in over forty collective exhibitions in Puerto Rico and abroad. His work expresses social and political themes in a sarcastic manner.

inventory.name: Manuel Rodríguez – Colección Reyes Veray

Manuel Rodríguez
 (Bayamón, PR, 1982)
En el 2008 obtuvo un Bachillerato en Escultura en la Escuela de Artes Plásticas de Puerto Rico. Ha sido merecedor de varias importantes distinciones. En el 2010 obtuvo la prestigiosa Beca Lexus con las Artes para el desarrollo de un proyecto que será expuesto en septiembre 2011 en el Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico. Ese mismo año ganó el Tercer Premio en el Certamen de Arte Joven de Oriental Bank. En el 2008 fue galardonado con el Premio Randy Barceló por su destacada labor en el Departamento de Escultura de la Escuela de Artes Plásticas y fue becado por la misma institución para viajar a La Feria Arco, España. Ha colaborado y asistido a los artistas Charles Juhasz Alvarado, Ramón Berríos y Adelino González. Actualmente trabaja desde su estudio/taller en Santurce y participa activamente en la escena plástica local.
Manuel Rodríguez (Bayamón, PR, 1982)
In 2008 he obtained a Bachelor’s Degree in Sculpture at the Escuela de Artes Plásticas de Puerto Rico. He has received several important distinctions. In 2010 he obtained the prestigious Lexus Scholarship with the Arts for the development of a project that will be exhibited in September 2011 at the Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico. That same year he won the Third Prize in the Young Art Contest of Oriental Bank. In 2008 he was awarded the Randy Barceló Prize for his outstanding work in the Sculpture Department of the Escuela de Artes Plásticas and was granted a scholarship by the same institution to travel to the Arco Fair, Spain. He has collaborated and assisted artists Charles Juhasz Alvarado, Ramón Berríos and Adelino González. He currently works from his studio/workshop in Santurce and actively participates in the local art scene.

inventory.name: Epifanio Irizarry – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Epifanio Irizarry
 (Ponce, PR, 1915 – 2001)
Pintor, ilustrador y profesor. Estudió con los pintores ponceños Horacio Castaing, Librado Net y Miguel Pou. Fue alistado en el ejército del general Patton y enviado a Austria y Francia. En la década del cincuenta estudió en la Liga de Estudiantes de Arte de Nueva York, donde fue discípulo de Reginald Marsh y Robert Brackman, entre otros. A su regreso a Puerto Rico, se incorporó al Taller de Gráfica de la División de Educación a la Comunidad (Divedco), donde trabajó como ilustrador hasta 1963. Posteriormente regresó a su ciudad natal para dedicarse por completo a la pintura y la enseñanza del arte. Entre otros reconocimientos, recibió el American International Academy Award y el Guggenheim Memorial Foundation Grant. Su obra aborda la temática costumbrista, presentando escenas del folklore y el paisaje puertorriqueño. Inspirándose en su pueblo natal, pintó estampas como los bailes de bomba y plena, el carnaval y el paisaje costero. Su obra se caracteriza por la sobriedad del color y la monocromía, así como su pincelada suelta y expresiva.
Epifanio Irizarry
 (Ponce, PR, 1915 – 2001)
Painter, illustrator and professor. He studied with Ponce painters Horacio Castaing, Librado Net, and Miguel Pou. He was drafted into General Patton’s army and sent to Austria and France. During the fifties, he studied at the New York League of Art Students under Reginald Marsh and Robert Brackman, among others. Upon his return to Puerto Rico, he joined the Graphics Studio of the Community Education Division (DIVEDCO), where he worked as illustrator until 1963. He later returned to his hometown to devote himself entirely to painting and teaching art. Among other recognitions, he has received the American International Academy Award and the Guggenheim Memorial Foundation Grant. His work deals with everyday themes, presenting folkloric scenes and the Puerto Rican landscape. Inspired by his hometown, he painted scenes such as bomba and plena dances, carnival, and the coastal landscape. Monochromatic and sober colors characterize his work, as well as his loose and expressive brushstrokes.

inventory.name: Teatro Tapia – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Teatro Tapia, San Juan – 1976
History of the Building
Municipal Theater 
Alejandro Tapia & Rivera
Construction of the San Juan Municipal Theater, one of the oldest in the Western Hemisphere and among the richest in cultural tradition and achievements, was begun in 1824 under the Spanish governorship of Don Miguel de la Torre, Count of Torrepando, and its design and construction are attributed to Don José Navarro y Herrera, Commander of Engineers.
Built of heavy adobe masonry and tamped rubble, with wood beams and timber trusses supporting a tin-clad gabled roof, and louvered windows and turned-wood stair and balcony railings, it was done in the prevailing primitive colonial style of the period reminiscent of the Tuscan neoclassical, and was probably inspired on La Scala de Milán.
It was a rather austere building, lacking in facilities and with unfinished exteriors except for its main façade, which was rich in neo-classical detail and which fortunately was but slightly altered during subsequent renovations, and its interior of which the outstanding feature was the excellent ceiling frescoes and painted proscenium decorations by Jenaro Pérez Villamil, reputedly a gifted apprentice of Goya.
In 1879, after suffering extensive damage from earthquakes and hurricanes, its first reconstruction was entrusted to Tulio Larrinaga, a brilliant Puerto Rican engineer versed in the design of cast iron and steel structures who gutted-out the interior and rebuilt it in the style of “La Belle Epoque”, with paired cast iron columns supporting the balconies, wrought iron lattice railings, and with iron staircases.
The structure remained basically unchanged until 1946 when, after several years of disuse, Architect Jorge Juliá Passarell undertook its renovation. At that time neither the community nor the authorities recognized the character and value of the architecture of the San Juan Historic Zone, and the design program called for a reconstruction with the interiors done in the “Art-Deco” style of the war time years. However debatable, it nonetheless provided an extended lease on life for the venerable structure which had already been scheduled for total demolition and whose utility had since been supplanted by the theater at the University of Puerto Rico.
A fly-loft, rigging, stage lighting and sound equipment, and an air conditioning system were installed for the first time in the theater. These systems were still in use, although obsolete and in need of extensive and costly repairs, until January of 1974 when the house was finally closed for restoration.
After two years of intensive design and construction, and at a cost of approximately two million dollars; the San Juan Municipal Theater reopened its doors to the community on December 28, 1976.
The design program called for the historical restoration of the existing structure and the installation of specialized theatrical equipment and electrical and mechanical systems in accordance with the latest advancements in the state of the art.
The design process involved extensive and analysis, and evaluation thereof, whereby the resulting project would represent an equilibrium between acceptable standards of historical authenticity and the demands of an intensely varied repertory theater-auditorium requiring complete changes of lighting, sound, and scenery plans on a weekly basis. Thus, data obtained through historical investigation was constantly being weighed against the possible options of an architecturally correct solution.
It was not the intention of the Architects nor of the Client to restore the building in all faithfulness to its original plan and stylistic detail, but rather to enhance and preserve its character while enabling it to function as an active, living organism capable of generating tremendous cultural activity in the community.
Technical Information:
1. Stage Lighting System: A completely transistorized an automated stage lighting system composed of a control console with memory-record capabilities and over ninety programmable presents, a dimmer bank with modular type transistorized dimmers, and interconnection panel, and quartz lighting fixtures.
2. Sound System: A multi-amplifier sound system controlled through an 
interconnection panel and mixer, permitting simultaneous recording, mixing, stage effects, previewing, monitoring, paging and play-back at any number of selected locations, and line intercom and cueing system for production personnel.
3. Rigging System: A 45-set counterweighted tee-track system with 2:1 reduction permitting operation from a fly gallery above the stage and with capabilities for reflecting stage panels, and an ample number of stage sets and backdrops.
4. Air Conditioning System: Separate systems permitting use only as required at the principal areas, such as house, offices, ticket booth, etc., and with a separate system for the stage to be used during rehearsals.
5. Electrical System: An independent electrical substation with capacity for all foreseen 
electrical loads, and an emergency battery system ensuring safe illumination of all areas in the event of power failures.
6. Fire Protection System: Increased number of fire exists, fire hoses, and the installation of an asbestos fire curtain at the proscenium which can be released manually, or automatically with heat-sensitive fusible links.
Architectural Features:
1. Construction of the west arcade where the sidewalk café is located with the lounge on the floor above. The foundations for this structure, which balances a similar one at the apposite side of the building, were laid by the original builders but construction was never completed.
2. Construction of a basement backstage where the workshop, storage areas, kitchen, and other services are located.
3. Relocation of the main staircases from the main lobby where they had been rebuilt during de renovation of 1949 to their original location in the lateral galleries, permitting the restoration of the wall openings of the front elevation and adjacent corners. The stairs now inter-connect all three levels of the theater.
4. Construction of the house ceiling in neo-classical style with a crystal chandelier as its focal point, and with contemporary stage lighting, sound and air conditioning equipment integrated in the design.
5. Restoration of the proscenium boxes which had been sealed for use as mechanical equipment ducts.
6. Restoration and completion of the building exterior, with a mansard screen commencing at the point of the original parapet elevation and extending over the fly-loft and other concrete structures added subsequently.
7. Reorganization of the interior spaces within the limitations imposed by the existing structure.
8. Installation of theater seating which was specially designed and fabricated with ornamental cast iron standards in order to preserve the integrity of period design.
9. Acoustics – The intended use of the building encompasses the entire range of the theatrical and musical arts as well as lectures and other assemblies of a civic nature. In planning the acoustical response of the house, and in the selection of materials, it was determined that optimum reflection from the ceiling and dispersion from the walls would ensure uniformity of sound distribution throughout the house, but that carpeted floors and upholstered seats would also be required in order to avoid excessive reverberation time and fluctuations in response between a full and an empty house. The house, as planned, is crisp with a medium-to-low reverberation time with permits clarity of the spoken voice without detracting from the brilliance and natural sonority of musical instruments. At present, during musical performances some of the sound is lost in the permanently flown rigging over the stage. However, once the sound reflecting stage panels, which were deleted from the original contract for financial reasons, are installed, this condition should be entirely corrected.

inventory.description:
Roberto Moya
 (Nueva York, EU, 1932 – Boston, EU, 2008)
Pintor y artista gráfico. Estudió en Eastern New Mexico University, Pratt Graphic Arts Center de Brooklyn, New School for Social Research de Nueva York, New York Phoenix School of Design y University of Southern California. Se ha presentado en numerosas de exhibiciones en Puerto Rico y el extranjero, incluyendo una exposición retrospectiva en Hawaii en 1998. En 1989 hizo el primer portafolio digital en Puerto Rico, por el cual fue invitado a dirigir un seminario en el Pratt Graphic Center. A principios de la década del noventa impartió cursos en la Universidad de Puerto Rico como artista residente. Utilizaba la computadora para hacer exploraciones de color antes de intervenir en la tela. Su obra, de estilo semiabstracto, se caracteriza por una amplia pincelada cargada de pigmento.
Roberto Moya
 (New York, US, 1932 – Boston, US, 2008)
Painter and graphic artist. He studied at the University of Eastern New Mexico, the Pratt Graphic Arts Center in Brooklyn, the New School for Social Research in New York, the New York Phoenix School of Design, and the University of Southern California. He has participated in numerous exhibitions in Puerto Rico and abroad, including a retrospective exhibition in Hawaii in 1998. In 1989, he prepared the first digital portfolio in Puerto Rico, for which he received an invitation to lead a workshop at the Pratt Graphic Center. In the early nineties, he taught courses at the University of Puerto Rico as resident artist. He uses his computer for color exploration before working on fabric. His semi-abstract work is characterized by broad, pigment-saturated brushstrokes.

inventory.name: Rolando López Dirube – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Rolando López Dirube
 (La Habana, Cuba, 1928 – San Juan, PR, 1997)
Escultor. Estudió en las facultades de Ingeniería y Arquitectura de la Universidad de La Habana, Cuba. Prosiguió estudios en Art Students’ League y en Brooklyn Museum Art School en Nueva York, bajo la supervisión de Gabor Peterdi, George Gras y Max Bekman. Ampliando su formación académica en la Escuela Nacional de Artes Gráficas y la Escuela de Artes de San Fernando en Madrid. Se desempeñó como profesor de análisis de diseño, pintura y escultura de la Escuela de Arquitectura de la Universidad de Puerto Rico, Universidad Interamericana de Puerto Rico, la Liga de Arte de San Juan y la Universidad del Sagrado Corazón. Gran parte de su obra se basó en conceptos matemáticos y geométricos.
Rolando López Dirube (Havana, Cuba, 1928 – San Juan, PR, 1997)
Sculptor. Studied at the faculties of Engineering and Architecture at the University of Havana, Cuba. He continued his studies at the Art Students’ League and at the Brooklyn Museum Art School in New York, under the supervision of Gabor Peterdi, George Gras and Max Bekman. He furthered his academic training at the Escuela Nacional de Artes Gráficas and the Escuela de Artes de San Fernando in Madrid. He served as professor of design analysis, painting and sculpture at the School of Architecture of the University of Puerto Rico, Interamerican University of Puerto Rico, the Art League of San Juan and the University of the Sacred Heart. Much of his work was based on mathematical and geometric concepts.

inventory.name: Sylvia Espinet – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Sylvia Espinet
 (San Juan, PR, 1932)
Ceramista. Sus primeros estudios fueron en Washington Irving School donde estudió diseño y costura, floristería y repostería. Tuvo su propia floristería y se dedicó por un tiempo a las manualidades, hasta que de forma autodidacta comenzó a explorar la cerámica y decidió tomar cursos. Estudió en la Liga de Estudiantes de Arte de San Juan, Casa Candina, Escuela de Artes Plásticas y la Universidad de Puerto Rico. También asistió a talleres en Nuevo México, Tampa y Puerto Rico (en el taller de Toni Hambleton). Trabajó por muchos años en su propio taller en Carraízo, Trujillo Alto. Impartió clases como voluntaria en escuelas públicas del país logrando exhibir el trabajo de sus estudiantes; de igual forma trabajó en Art & Clay Studio en Nuevo México. En 1994 una de sus piezas fue escogida para la Muestra del Quinto Centenario. Museo del Arsenal de la Puntilla, ICP. Ganadora del Popular Ceramics Highest Award en Orlando, Florida. Ha exhibido en Puerto Rico, México, Venezuela, República Dominicana, Estados Unidos y Brasil. En su trabajo escultórico trabaja las esferas a través de las cuales explora el mundo.
Sylvia Espinet
 (San Juan, P.R., 1932)
Ceramist. She first studied at the Washington Irving School where she studied design and sewing, flower arrangement, and fine pastry-making. She owned a flower shop and spent some time creating arts and crafts, until she began exploring ceramics on her own and decided to take some courses. She studied at the San Juan League of Art Students, Casa Candina, the School of Plastic Arts, and the University of Puerto Rico. She also attended workshops in New Mexico, Tampa, and Puerto Rico (at the Toni Hambleton workshop). For many years she had her own workshop in Carraizo, Trujillo Alto. She was a volunteer teacher in the Puerto Rico public schools and was able to exhibit her students’ work; similarly, she worked at the Art & Clay Studio in New Mexico. In 1954 one of her pieces was chosen for inclusion in the Fifth Centenary Exhibit. She won the Popular Ceramics Highest Award in Orlando, Florida. Her work has been shown in Puerto Rico, Mexico, Venezuela, Dominican Republic, the United States, and Brazil. Her sculptural work deals with the spheres through which she explores the world.

inventory.name: Noemí Ruiz – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Noemí Ruiz
 (Mayagüez, PR, 1931 – 2023)
Pintora, artista gráfica y profesora. Obtuvo un Bachillerato en Artes de la Universidad Interamericana de San Germán, una Maestría en Artes en New York University y cursó estudios doctorales en la Universidad Central de Madrid, España. Fue discípula de George McNeill y estudiante de litografía en el Taller de la Asociación de Estudiantes de la Universidad de California en Berkley. Se desempeñó como Directora del Departamento de Bellas Artes en la Universidad Interamericana de Puerto Rico en San Germán. Fue catedrática distinguida del Recinto Metropolitano de la UIA. Es socia fundadora del Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Puerto Rico y miembro de la Junta Directiva de la Escuela de Artes Plásticas de Puerto Rico, donde también ha ejercido como profesora. Ha recibido múltiples premios y reconocimientos entre los que se encuentran el Primer Premio en Pintura del Certamen del Ateneo Puertorriqueño en 1974; Mujer Distinguida en las Bellas Artes, Gobierno de Puerto Rico, 1979; entre otros. Es una figura clave en el desarrollo del arte abstracto en Puerto Rico. Su obra se caracteriza por composiciones formales de abstracción lírica, con gran dominio del color y en las cuales el elemento conceptual personal y de la naturaleza está simbólicamente presente.
Noemí Ruiz
 (Mayagüez, PR, 1931 – 2023)
Painter, graphic artist, and professor. She obtained a Bachelor of Arts from Inter American University in San Germán and a Master of Arts from New York University, and pursued doctoral studies at the Universidad Central de Madrid in Spain. She was a student of George McNeill and studied lithography at the Student Association Workshop at the University of California, Berkley. She was Director of the Fine Arts Department at Inter American University in San Germán, and a renowned professor at its Metropolitan campus. She is a founding member of the Puerto Rico Museum of Contemporary Art and a member of the Board of Directors of the Puerto Rico School of Plastic Arts, where she has also worked as a professor. She has received numerous awards and recognitions, including First Prize in Painting at the Ateneo Puertorriqueño Competition in 1974, and was selected Outstanding Woman of the Fine Arts by the government of Puerto Rico in 1979. She is a key figure in the development of abstract art in Puerto Rico. Her work is characterized by lyrically abstract formal compositions which reveal an extensive mastery of color, and in which a conceptual personal and natural element are symbolically present.

inventory.name: Marta Pérez – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
Marta Pérez
 (San Juan, PR, 1934 – 2004)
Pintora y profesora. En 1955 obtuvo un Bachillerato en Arte y Filosofía en Notre Dame College de Maryland, que la becó para estudiar en Roma por un año. En 1977 estudió pintura al óleo y dibujo con el profesor Larry Gluck en Los Ángeles, California. Ofreció clases de arte en la Administración de Veteranos y en la Universidad de Puerto Rico y fue Directora de arte en Caribbean Consolidated Schools. Colaboró con el maestro ceramista Hal Lasky en el taller de cerámica Puerto Rican Pottery. Desde principios de los ochenta hasta el día de su muerte se dedicó por completo a su obra en su taller del Viejo San Juan. Su obra se caracteriza por el exuberante colorido, la aglomeración de elementos y las figuras femeninas de aspecto mítico y angelical.
Marta Pérez
 (San Juan, PR, 1934 – 2004)
Painter and professor. In 1955 she received a Bachelor of Arts in Art and Philosophy from Notre Dame College in Maryland, where she was awarded a scholarship to study in Rome for one year. In 1977 she studied oil painting and drawing with professor Larry Gluck in Los Angeles, California. She taught art at the Veterans Administration and the University of Puerto Rico, and was Art Director at Caribbean Consolidated Schools. She collaborated with master ceramist Hal Lasky in the Puerto Rican Pottery ceramics studio. Since the early eighties until her death, she devoted herself entirely to working in her studio in Old San Juan. Her work is characterized by exuberant colors, the agglomeration of elements, and female figures of mythical or angelical appearance.

inventory.name: David Alvarez – Colección Reyes Veray
inventory.description:
David Álvarez
 (San Juan, PR, 1972)
David Álvarez nació, creció y sigue viviendo en Puerto Rico. Álvarez comenzó publicando tirillas cómicas y viñetas en periódicos y revistas locales, y luego exploró el mundo del cómic autopublicando una serie de un superhéroe de dibujos animados llamado ‘Changuy’ y también trabajó y desarrolló algunos proyectos locales de animación. Su siguiente creación fue ‘Yenny López’, que comenzó en Primera Hora en 2002 y se distribuye en Estados Unidos a través de Universal Uclick. En 2007, ‘Kike Koki’ se publicó en el periódico El Nuevo Día durante cuatro años.
Álvarez es un artista independiente para Warner Brothers Worldwide Publishing y su trabajo puede verse en los cómics de ‘Looney Tunes’ como dibujante. Colaboró con la escritora Gail Simone en una historia corta publicada en ‘9-11: Emergency Relief”. También ilustra storyboards para la serie de animación de Warner Brothers “Krypto the Superdog”. En 2010, dibujó el cómic “Muppet King Arthur” para Boom Studios, protagonizado por Los Teleñecos de Jim Henson.
www.dascomics.com
David Álvarez
 (San Juan, PR, 1972)
David Alvarez was born, raised and still lives in Puerto Rico. Alvarez started publishing comic strips and cartoons in local newspapers and magazines, and then explored the comic book world by self-publishing a series of a humorous cartoon superhero called ‘Changuy’ and also worked and developed a few local animated projects. His next creation was ‘Yenny Lopez’, that started in Primera Hora in 2002 and is distributed in the USA through Universal Uclick. In 2007, ‘Kike Koki’ was published in the newspaper El Nuevo Día for four years.
Alvarez is a freelance artist for Warner Brothers Worldwide Publishing and his work can be seen in ‘Looney Tunes’ comics as a penciller. He cooperated with writer Gail Simone on a short story published in ‘9-11: Emergency Relief’. He also illustrates storyboards for Warner Brothers animated series ‘Krypto the Superdog’. In 2010, he drew the comic book ‘Muppet King Arthur’ for Boom Studios, starring Jim Henson’s The Muppets.
www.lambiek.net/artists/a/alvarez_david…

inventory.description:
Charles-Édouard Jeanneret-Gris (Le Corbusier )
 (Suiza, 1887- Francia, 1965)
Arquitecto y escritor. Famoso por sus contribuciones a lo que hoy se le conoce como Arquitectura Moderna. A sus treinta años se convirtió en ciudadano francés. Fue el pionero del estudio teórico del diseño moderno y se dedicó a proveer una mejor condición de vida para los residentes de las grandes ciudades. Su carrera se extendió sobre cinco décadas, con sus edificios icónicos construidos en Europa central, India, Rusia, Norteamérica y Suramérica. También se dedicó a la planificación urbana, a la pintura, escultura y al diseño muebles modernos.
Charles-Édouard Jeanneret-Gris (Le Corbusier )
 (Switzerland, 1887- France, 1965)
Architect and writer. Famous for his contributions to what is known today as Modern Architecture. In his thirties he became a French citizen. He pioneered the theoretical study of modern design and dedicated himself to providing better living conditions for the residents of large cities. His career spanned over five decades, with his iconic buildings constructed in Central Europe, India, Russia, North America and South America. He was also involved in urban planning, painting, sculpture and modern furniture design.

Abismael (Aby) Ruiz (Arecibo, PR, 1971)

His work reflects an expressionist character with social themes.

Frances Gallardo

inventory.description:
Garvin Sierra
 (Ponce, PR, 1977)
Escultor, grabador y nuevos medios. Obtuvo un Bachillerato en Bellas Artes con concentración en Escultura y Artes Gráficas de la Universidad de Puerto Rico, Recinto de Río Piedras. Durante sus años de formación trabajó como asistente de escultores como Melquiades Rosario Sastre, Ramón Berríos y Soucy de Perellano. Paralelo a su trabajo como artista plástico, Sierra Vega se desempeña actualmente como diseñador gráfico independiente y diseñador de exhibiciones. Algunas de las distinciones de las cuales ha sido merecedor incluyen: Primer Premio Cartel por “Retorno 1903-2003, Universidad de Puerto Rico, Recinto de Río Piedras y Mención de Honor en el Certamen de Artes Plásticas del Ateneo Puertorriqueño (ambas en el 2001); Primer Premio de Diseño, Copa Bombay Sapphire (2003); Primer Premio Colectiva de Artistas Puertorriqueños, 26a Bienal de Gráfica, Ljubljana, Eslovenia (2005) y Mención de Honor Certamen de Arte Joven Oriental Group (2009). Su obra ha sido exhibida internacionalmente en países como Argentina, Colombia, Japón, Eslovenia, México, Portugal y Estados Unidos, entre otros, y forma parte de prestigiosas colecciones privadas e institucionales como el Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Puerto Rico (MAC), Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico (MAPR) y el Museo de Historia, Antropología y Arte de la Universidad de Puerto Rico (MHAA). Su obra es reconocida por sus grabados y esculturas de crítica social, política y de conflictos bélicos.
Garvin Sierra
 (Ponce, PR, 1977)
Sculptor, graphic and new media artist. He earned a Bachelor’s degree in Fine Arts with a concentration in Sculpture and Graphic Arts at Universidad de Puerto Rico, Río Piedras Campus. During his formative years he worked as assistant to sculptors such as Melquíades Rosario Sastre, Ramón Berríos and Perellano Soucy. Parallel to his work as an artist, Sierra Vega serves currently as a freelance graphic designer and as a designer of exhibitions. Some distinctions he has been worthy of include: First Prize Poster for “Retorno 1903-2003”, Universidad de Puerto Rico, Río Piedras Campus and an Honorable Mention in Certamen de Artes Plásticas of Ateneo Puertorriqueño (both in 2001); First Prize for Design, Bombay Sapphire Cup (2003); First Prize for Puerto Rican Artists Collective, 26th Graphics Biennial, Ljubljana, Slovenia (2005) and Honorable Mention at Certamen de Arte Joven, Oriental Group (2009). His work has been exhibited internationally in countries such as Argentina, Colombia, Japan, Slovenia, Mexico, Portugal and United States, among others, and is part of prestigious private and institutional collections such as Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Puerto Rico (MAC), Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico (MAPR) and  Museo de Historia, Antropología y Arte de la Universidad de Puerto Rico (MHAA). His work is recognized for his prints and sculptures of social, political and military conflicts criticism.

Irene Delano
 (Detroit, MI, EEUU, 1919 – San Juan, P.R., 1982)
Diseñadora gráfica, ilustradora de libros, cartelista y maestra. Estudió en la Academia de Bellas Artes de Filadelfia, Estados Unidos. En 1941 se trasladó a Puerto Rico junto a su esposo, Jack Delano. Fundó en 1946 el Taller de Cinema y Gráfica de Parques y Recreo Público, que dirigió hasta 1952. Este luego se transformó en la División de Educación de la Comunidad. Hasta el momento de su muerte trabajó en su taller como diseñadora de revistas, libros, folletos y carteles. Algunos de los artistas que trabajaron bajo su dirección fueron: Manuel Hernández Acevedo, Rafael Tufiño, Julio Rosado del Valle, Lorenzo Homar y Félix Bonilla Norat.
Irene Delano
 (Detroit, US, 1919 – San Juan, P.R., 1982)
Graphic designer, book illustrator, poster designer, and teacher. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Philadelphia, United States. In 1941 she moved to Puerto Rico with her husband Jack Delano. In 1946 she established the Cinema and Graphics for Parks and Public Recreation Workshop, which she directed until 1952. The Workshop later became the Community Education Division. She remained productive until her death, working at her workshop designing magazines, books, pamphlets, and posters. Some of the artists who worked under her direction are: Manuel Hernández Acevedo, Rafael Tufiño, Julio Rosado del Valle, Lorenzo Homar, and Félix Bonilla Norat.
